### Summary

## Observed behavior

I have hosts file configured like this:
```
[linux-hosts]
linux-0 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.16.119'"
linux-1 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.19.183'"
linux-2 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.19.21'"
linux-3 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.17.208'"

linux-5 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.16.110'"
linux-6 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.19.235'"
linux-7 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.18.255'"
linux-8 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.18.165'"
linux-9 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.16.94'"
```

When I run my playbook against any individual host using `--limit linux-X`, it is completely fine. 

However, when I run it agains all hosts, everything is done on a single host, although Ansible reports connecting to multiple hosts. I've found out the hard way, apt locks were not obtained for no obvious reson:
```
TASK [setup : Update and upgrade apt packages] **********************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************************
fatal: [linux-0]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-2]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-3]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-4]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-6]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-8]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-5]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-7]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}
fatal: [linux-9]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "Failed to lock apt for exclusive operation"}

changed: [linux-1]
```

But then I've verified that all connections were made to a single machine, so only one obtained the lock and the rest failed.

## Expected behavior:

When I have multiple hosts configured with ProxyCommand, I expect each host to use its own configuration.



### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

Inventory

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
ansible 2.9.27
  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/user/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3.8/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.8.12 (default, Aug 31 2021, 01:23:42) [GCC]
```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed
# no changes
```


### OS / Environment

OpenSUSE Tumbleweed

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->

Create this hosts file:
```yaml (paste below)
[linux-hosts]
linux-0 ansible_host=192.168.0.3 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test ansible_ssh_common_args="-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ProxyCommand='ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_test -W %h:%p ubuntu@10.0.16.119'"

```

Run `ansible linux* -i inventory/hosts -m setup | grep macaddress`


### Expected Results

I expect the ansible to connect do distinct machines using the ProxyCommand. There should be different MAC addresses reported.

### Actual Results

```console

            "macaddress": "fa:16:3e:46:e0:96",

```

```
